feed.title: APM Overflow
feed.subtitle: Hey, I'm Islam. I was born and raised between Egypt and Saudi Arabia, but I'm currently based in Durham, NC studying CS at Duke. In high school, I played osu...

entry.title: On Agent Memory Fidelity (Decant)
entry.content: Since Sonnet 3.7 came out right before my last internship, I’ve barely hand-written code. Coding agents are getting insanely good, and I keep trusting these models to do more and more. I think we’re heading toward a world where most (if not all) code is written through and by agents.

entry.title: On Fingerspitzengefühl
entry.content: I used to play this rhythm game called osu! from ages 11 to 17. You might've seen clips of people reacting to it. The concept is simple: you click circles to the beat of a song. Most players aim with a graphic tablet and tap with Z + X on their keyboard. I played semi-competitively around 2020-2022.

entry.title: On Dimensions of Taste (Harmonia)
entry.content: Over last semester, I wanted to see whether I could formalize my music preferences numerically, whether I could model the distinctions I felt but couldn't articulate, and use them to automatically sort my liked songs into playlists. Could I build something that surfaces patterns in my library I sense but can't describe?

entry.title: On Closing Doors
entry.content: Much of our fears stem from uncertainty. It's then intuitive to keep as many doors open just in case, and meeting freshmen who want to concurrently "build and apply to YC" and "keep quant as a backup" suggests this hedging impulse is more foundational.

entry.title: On Using Computers
entry.content: I remember figuring out the shortest routes to class first semester of college. The lowkey flex of "I know a quicker way" never saved much time, and yet it felt fun to explore campus through these mildly competitive treks.
